definitionEn: a situation or area in which groups compete or argue fiercely
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение — сфера острой борьбы или споров; буквальное «поле боя» проще.
situation: You describe a topic, market or place where rival groups compete or argue with great intensity.

examples.text: School history lessons have become a political [[battlefield]], with each new government rewriting the textbooks.
Every evening our living room turns into a [[battlefield]] over who gets the TV remote.
Their divorce quickly became a legal [[battlefield]], with each side accusing the other of hiding money.

texts: For years, the kitchen was a [[battlefield]] between my two teenage sons.
The smartphone market is a crowded [[battlefield]] where only the biggest players survive.
Online comment sections often turn into a [[battlefield]] of insults and angry opinions.

badCollocation.noteRu: Побеждают в битве — win the battle. Battlefield — это место или сфера борьбы, его не «выигрывают».

collocationTask.prompt: the meeting quickly ___ into a battlefield
collocationTask.explanationRu: Превратиться во что-то — turn into: the meeting turned into a battlefield. Become into — ошибка, made into требует дополнения, went into значит «вошёл».

nuance.text: Every family dinner turns into a [[battlefield]] once my uncles start shouting about football.
nuance.explanationRu: Battlefield — открытая борьба и споры. Minefield — ситуация со скрытыми опасностями, где легко ошибиться. Когда все уже кричат и спорят, это battlefield.

reverse.text: Employment law is a [[minefield]]: one tiny mistake can cost a company thousands.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о скрытом риске ошибиться, а не об открытой борьбе, поэтому minefield.

fixIt.text: Three rival coffee shops opening at once turned our quiet street into a [[battle]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Улица — это место, поэтому она превращается в battlefield (поле битвы), а не в battle (саму битву).

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "How did the budget meeting go?"
options: Great, it was a real battlefield — everyone agreed with everything.
Honestly, it was a battlefield. Every department fought for every penny.
It constituted a battlefield of considerable magnitude, one might say.
reply.explanationRu: Battlefield — место острой борьбы, а не согласия. Третий вариант слишком книжный для сообщения коллеге.

definitionEn: a narrow line of light or energy coming from a torch, lamp or laser
senseNote: Выбрано значение «луч (фонаря, фар, лазера)»; не путайте с beam — «балка, брус».
situation: A torch, car headlight, lighthouse or laser sends out a narrow line of light.

examples.text: When the lights went down, a single [[beam]] lit up the singer in the centre of the stage.
The alarm goes off as soon as anyone breaks the infrared [[beam]] across the doorway.
Every ten seconds, the lighthouse sent a bright [[beam]] sweeping across the dark sea.

texts: The surgeon used a laser [[beam]] to correct the patient's short sight.
The fox froze in the [[beam]] of our torch, then vanished into the bushes.
On empty country roads at night, it's safe to drive on full [[beam]].

badCollocation.noteRu: «Луч надежды» — a ray of hope. Beam — физический луч от фонаря, фар, маяка или лазера.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Дальний свет фар — full beam (в американском варианте — high beams). Ray, shine и glow в этом выражении не используются.

nuance.text: The security guard swept the [[beam]] of his torch across the empty car park.
nuance.explanationRu: Beam — направленный луч от фонаря, фар, маяка или лазера. Ray — солнечный луч или излучение (UV rays), а также a ray of hope. У фонаря — beam.

reverse.text: Sunscreen protects your skin from the sun's harmful [[rays]].
reverse.explanationRu: Об излучении солнца говорят rays: UV rays, the sun's rays. Beams — лучи от фонаря, фар или лазера.

fixIt.text: At last the lost hikers saw the [[ray]] of a searchlight moving across the hillside.
fixIt.explanationRu: Луч прожектора, фонаря или фар — beam. Ray — о солнечных лучах и в выражении a ray of hope.

reply.context: You're a passenger in a car at night. The driver says: "I can hardly see the road. There are no street lights here."
options: Why not put the headlights on full beam? There's nobody coming.
Just hold on to a beam of hope. We'll get there eventually.
It would be advisable to activate the vehicle's maximum beam function forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Дальний свет — full beam. «Beam of hope» — ошибка (нужно ray of hope), а третий вариант звучит как инструкция, а не как слова пассажира.

definitionEn: a thing or situation of a particular kind, especially a difficult or powerful one
senseNote: Здесь — разговорное «штука, вещь (особого рода)», как в a different beast; значение «зверь, животное» проще.
situation: You compare two activities or systems and stress that one is much harder or quite unlike the other.

examples.text: Managing people is a completely different [[beast]] from writing good code.
His new motorbike is a powerful [[beast]] that can reach 100 km/h in three seconds.
Live television is an unpredictable [[beast]]: anything can go wrong at any moment.

texts: Running a marathon is a very different [[beast]] from jogging round the park.
Late nights before a launch are simply the nature of the [[beast]] in advertising.
Our old car was a noisy [[beast]], but it never once broke down.

badCollocation.noteRu: Устойчивое выражение — the nature of the beast («такова специфика»). Character в нём не используется.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Совсем другое дело» — a different beast altogether (или entirely). At all бывает только в отрицаниях и вопросах, а fully и absolutely так не ставят.

nuance.text: If you work in retail, weekend shifts are just the nature of the [[beast]].
nuance.explanationRu: The nature of the beast («такова специфика») — неизменное выражение, animal в нём не используется, хотя a different animal (амер.) и a different beast — синонимы.

reverse.text: My brother is a real party [[animal]]: he's out every weekend.
reverse.explanationRu: Party animal — устойчивое выражение о любителе вечеринок; party beast так не говорят.

fixIt.text: Writing a novel is a completely different [[case]] from writing short stories.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Совсем другое дело» — a completely different beast (разг.) или matter. Case — это «случай», в таком значении не используется.

reply.context: A friend who has just started managing a team messages you: "Leading people is so much harder than doing the actual work!"
options: Your team must be a real beast. Do they bite?
Totally different beast, right? It gets easier with time.
Indeed, managerial duties constitute a separate beast entirely.
reply.explanationRu: A different beast — «совсем другое дело», разговорное выражение. В первом ответе beast понят буквально как зверь, третий слишком официален для чата.

definitionEn: used after 'on' to mean acting for someone or as their representative
senseNote: Употребляется только в выражениях on behalf of someone и on someone's behalf.
situation: You speak, sign or act for another person or an organization, as their official representative.

examples.text: I'm writing on [[behalf]] of my manager, who is away until Monday.
The actor was ill, so his daughter accepted the award on his [[behalf]].
Volunteers collected money on [[behalf]] of a local children's hospital.

texts: The lawyer spoke on her [[behalf]] because she was too upset to talk.
On [[behalf]] of the whole team, thank you for your hard work this year.
Parents often have to make decisions on [[behalf]] of very young children.

badCollocation.noteRu: «От имени» — только on behalf of. Предлог from здесь — калька с русского «от».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Правильно только on behalf of («от имени»). From — калька с «от», in behalf of — устаревший американский вариант, by здесь невозможно.

nuance.text: Thank you for talking to the landlord on my [[behalf]] while I was away.
nuance.explanationRu: On my behalf — от моего имени, вместо меня. On my part — «с моей стороны», то есть то, что сделал я сам: a mistake on my part.

reverse.text: Sorry, that was a mistake on my [[part]]: I sent you the wrong file.
reverse.explanationRu: Ошибку совершил я сам, значит on my part («с моей стороны»). On my behalf — когда кто-то действует за меня.

fixIt.text: I'm writing on [[the part]] of all the tenants to complain about the broken heating.
fixIt.explanationRu: «От имени» жильцов — on behalf of. On the part of значит «со стороны» и указывает, кто совершил действие.

reply.context: Your manager calls: "I'm stuck in traffic. Can you start the client meeting without me?"
options: Sure. I'll welcome them on my behalf and tell them you're late.
No problem. Your behalf shall be duly represented forthwith.
Of course. I'll welcome them on your behalf and explain you're running late.
reply.explanationRu: Вы действуете за начальника, поэтому on your behalf. On my behalf — «от моего имени», а второй вариант звучит странно и слишком официально.

rewrite.original: My colleague spoke for me at the meeting because I was ill.
rewrite.frame: My colleague spoke ____ at the meeting because I was ill.
rewrite.explanationRu: Говорить за кого-то, от его имени — speak on someone's behalf.

definitionEn: loved very much and deeply valued by a person or by many people
situation: You describe a person, place or thing that someone, or a whole community, cares about deeply.

examples.text: The whole village came to the funeral of the [[beloved]] teacher who had taught three generations of local children.
The café has been a [[beloved]] part of the neighbourhood since 1952, and regulars are furious about its closure.
The finale killed off the show's most [[beloved]] character, and fans still haven't forgiven the writers.

texts: He took his [[beloved]] old guitar with him to every gig.
The park is [[beloved]] by joggers, dog walkers and families alike.
After thirty years abroad, she finally returned to her [[beloved]] Scotland.

badCollocation.noteRu: О любимом цвете, блюде или фильме говорят favourite. Beloved — глубоко любимый человек, место или вещь, звучит торжественно.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Beloved by — «любимый кем-то». Lovely — милый, lovable — обаятельный, loving — любящий; с by в этом смысле они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The singer is still [[beloved]] by fans who first heard her songs in the 1980s.
nuance.explanationRu: Beloved — тот, кого любят: beloved by fans. Loving — тот, кто любит сам: a loving mother. «Loving by fans» — ошибка.

reverse.text: She gave her son a [[loving]] hug before he got on the train.
reverse.explanationRu: Объятие выражает любовь, поэтому loving hug. Beloved описывает того, кого любят, а не действие.

fixIt.text: The old cinema, [[loving]] by students for its cheap tickets, is closing down next month.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кинотеатр любят студенты, значит он beloved by students. Loving — «любящий», так описывают того, кто любит сам.

reply.context: A friend messages: "They're closing the old bookshop on the corner!"
options: Oh no! The owner was always so beloved to customers. He gave everyone discounts.
Oh no, not that place! It's beloved by the whole neighbourhood.
Alas! My beloved emporium of literature shall be no more.
reply.explanationRu: Beloved by — «любимый кем-то», так и надо. В первом ответе beloved ошибочно значит «добрый к людям», а третий звучит как пародия на старинный роман.

rewrite.original: Millions of readers love her detective novels.
rewrite.frame: Her detective novels are ____ millions of readers.
rewrite.explanationRu: Beloved by + те, кто любит: beloved by millions of readers.

definitionEn: a standard or reference point used for measuring or judging quality or performance
situation: You compare results or products with an accepted standard to see how good they really are.

examples.text: Many schools use national exam results as a [[benchmark]] for measuring their own performance.
In independent tests, the new laptop scored well above the industry [[benchmark]] for battery life.
Her marathon time of 2 hours 20 minutes became the [[benchmark]] that every young runner aimed for.

texts: Last year's sales figures will serve as a [[benchmark]] for the new team.
This novel remains the [[benchmark]] against which all crime fiction is judged.
Investors compare their returns with a [[benchmark]] such as the national stock index.

collocations: the [[benchmark]] against which something is judged

badCollocation.noteRu: Планку или эталон устанавливают глаголом set: set a benchmark. Put с benchmark не сочетается.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Установить новый эталон — set a benchmark (как set a record или set a standard). Put, do и install с benchmark не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Her study became the [[benchmark]] against which all later research was measured.
nuance.explanationRu: Benchmark — эталон, с которым сравнивают и по которому измеряют. Landmark — ориентир на местности или поворотное событие (a landmark decision); им ничего не измеряют.

reverse.text: The court's [[landmark]] ruling changed the law on privacy.
reverse.explanationRu: Решение стало историческим, поворотным, поэтому landmark. Benchmark — только эталон для сравнения.

fixIt.text: We use last year's figures as a [[sample]] to measure how much we have improved.
fixIt.explanationRu: Эталон для сравнения — benchmark. Sample — «образец, проба» (a blood sample, a free sample), им прогресс не измеряют.

wordFormation.text: Regular [[benchmarking]] against competitors helps the firm spot its weaknesses early.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "How will we know if the new training programme is actually working?"
options: We could put a benchmark in the training room so people have somewhere to sit.
Let's use last year's customer scores as a benchmark and compare the results every month.
Yeah, we could, like, do a benchmark thing or whatever.
reply.explanationRu: Benchmark — эталон для сравнения, это и нужно. Первый ответ путает его со скамейкой (bench), а третий звучит небрежно для совещания.

definitionEn: not suitable for someone because it is too low for their status or character
senseNote: Здесь — «ниже достоинства» (it's beneath you); значение «под, внизу» — базовое.
situation: Someone refuses a task or behaviour because they think it is too low for their status or character.

examples.text: He thinks making coffee for visitors is [[beneath]] him, even though he's the newest intern.
Answering those rude comments would be [[beneath]] you, so just ignore them.
The senator said that responding to personal insults was [[beneath]] the dignity of her office.

texts: Cheating to win a board game against children is [[beneath]] you.
She considered a small part in a TV advert [[beneath]] her and turned it down.
Such cheap personal attacks are [[beneath]] a serious journalist.

collocations: feel that a job is [[beneath]] you

badCollocation.noteRu: С уровнями, оценками и цифрами используют below: below average, below zero. Beneath в переносном смысле — «ниже достоинства».

collocationTask.prompt: Lying about something so small is ___ you.
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Ниже твоего достоинства» — beneath you. Under и underneath — только о физическом положении, а lower than you — калька с русского.

nuance.text: Spreading gossip about a colleague is [[beneath]] you, and you know it.
nuance.explanationRu: Beneath someone — «ниже чьего-то достоинства». Below — про уровни, числа и положение: below zero, below average; в значении «недостойно» звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Last night the temperature dropped to ten degrees [[below]] zero.
reverse.explanationRu: О температуре и числах говорят below: below zero. Beneath так не используется.

fixIt.text: Replying to anonymous insults online is [[under]] your dignity.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Ниже достоинства» — beneath your dignity. Under — «под» в прямом смысле, с dignity не сочетается.

reply.context: A colleague complains: "The manager asked me to help sort the post today. I have a master's degree!"
options: Come on, no job is beneath you when the team is short-staffed.
Oh, then sorting post is beneath you, so you'll love it!
One observes that sorting post is situated beneath your qualifications.
reply.explanationRu: Beneath you — «ниже твоего достоинства»: никакая работа не зазорна. Во втором ответе смысл перепутан, третий звучит неестественно книжно.

rewrite.original: She thought that cleaning the office was not good enough for someone like her.
rewrite.frame: She thought that cleaning the office was ____.

definitionEn: a person or group that gains an advantage as a result of something
situation: A new law, trend or event helps a particular group, which ends up better off than before.

examples.text: Small farmers will be the main [[beneficiaries]] of the new trade agreement, which cuts taxes on their exports.
Children from low-income families were the biggest [[beneficiaries]] of the free school meals scheme.
Delivery companies were among the clearest [[beneficiaries]] of the lockdowns, as online orders doubled.

texts: The local economy was the main [[beneficiary]] of the music festival.
Every pupil in the school is a [[beneficiary]] of the new reading programme.
In the end, the only real [[beneficiary]] of the price war was the customer.

badCollocation.noteRu: После beneficiary нужен предлог of: the beneficiary of the reform. From сочетается с глаголом benefit: benefit from.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Главные выгодоприобретатели — the main (biggest, chief) beneficiaries. Large, strong и general с beneficiaries не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Ironically, the main [[beneficiary]] of the train strike was a small bike shop near the station.
nuance.explanationRu: Beneficiary — тот, кто выиграл от ситуации. Recipient — получатель чего-то конкретного (письма, награды, органа); от забастовки ничего не «получают».

reverse.text: At nineteen, she was the youngest [[recipient]] of the award.
reverse.explanationRu: Награду получают, поэтому recipient. Beneficiary — тот, кому ситуация принесла выгоду, а не получатель премии.

fixIt.text: Tourists will be the main [[benefactors]] of the new airport, as flights will get cheaper.
fixIt.explanationRu: Тот, кто получает выгоду, — beneficiary. Benefactor — наоборот, благотворитель, который даёт деньги.

reply.context: A friend asks: "So who actually gains from the new four-day week at your company?"
options: Our CEO is the main beneficiary. She's the one paying for all of it.
The beneficiary aspect is super beneficiary for all of us, basically.
Honestly, the biggest beneficiaries are parents with young kids.
reply.explanationRu: Beneficiaries — те, кто выигрывает, например родители. Тот, кто платит, не beneficiary, а второй ответ бессмысленно повторяет слово.

rewrite.original: The new policy helps first-time buyers more than anyone else.
rewrite.frame: First-time buyers are ____ of the new policy.

definitionEn: not harmful or dangerous, especially of a growth in the body that is not cancer
senseNote: Здесь — «безвредный, доброкачественный» (медицина, экология, IT); значение «добрый, мягкий» встречается реже.
situation: A doctor tells a patient that a lump is not cancer, or scientists say a substance causes no harm.

examples.text: Luckily, the tests showed that the lump on her neck was [[benign]].
The detergent is sold as eco-friendly because it contains only [[benign]] ingredients.
The antivirus flagged the file, but it turned out to be completely [[benign]].

texts: Most moles on the skin are [[benign]] and need no treatment at all.
Scientists believe the chemical is [[benign]] at such low doses.
Security software sometimes blocks perfectly [[benign]] programs by mistake.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Доброкачественный товар» — a high-quality product. Benign значит «не опасный» (об опухоли, веществе), а не «качественный».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Доброкачественная опухоль — a benign tumour. Kind, good и gentle — калька с «добро-», в медицине так не говорят.

nuance.text: Doctors removed the growth, and tests later confirmed it was [[benign]].
nuance.explanationRu: Benign — безвредный, доброкачественный (об опухоли, веществе). Benevolent — доброжелательный, щедрый; так говорят о людях, а не об опухолях.

fixIt.text: The scan showed that the tumour was [[good-quality]], so she didn't need chemotherapy.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Доброкачественная опухоль» — benign tumour. Good-quality значит «высокого качества» и говорится о товарах.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "Just got my test results. The doctor says the lump is nothing to worry about."
options: Oh no, it's benign? I'm so sorry. When does the treatment start?
Excellent. The benignity of your lump is hereby noted.
What a relief! So it's benign? That's the best news all week.
reply.explanationRu: Benign — «доброкачественная, не опасная», это хорошая новость. В первом ответе смысл перепутан, второй звучит как официальный протокол.

definitionEn: to show a feeling or fact that someone wants to hide, without meaning to
senseNote: Здесь — «невольно выдавать» (чувства, мысли); основное значение «предавать» проще.
situation: Someone tries to look calm, but their voice, face or hands show what they really feel.

examples.text: She answered every question calmly, but her shaking hands [[betrayed]] her nerves.
He claimed to be a local, but his accent [[betrayed]] his foreign origins.
Although she said she loved the gift, her face [[betrayed]] a hint of disappointment.

texts: His trembling voice [[betrayed]] how nervous he really was.
Not a single muscle in her face [[betrayed]] her surprise.
A slight hesitation [[betrayed]] his doubts about the plan.

badCollocation.noteRu: Благодарность выражают сознательно — express gratitude. Betray — невольно выдать то, что хочешь скрыть.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Голос её выдал» — her voice betrayed her (или gave her away). Showed, issued и told без дополнения так не употребляются.

nuance.text: He tried to act confident, but his voice [[betrayed]] him.
nuance.explanationRu: Betray someone — невольно выдать человека, его истинные чувства: his voice betrayed him. Reveal требует, что именно раскрыто (revealed his fear), и часто делается намеренно.

reverse.text: At the press conference, the company [[revealed]] its plans for a new factory.
reverse.explanationRu: Планы объявили намеренно, поэтому revealed. Betray — выдать невольно или раскрыть чужой секрет.

fixIt.text: She smiled and said she was fine, but her red eyes [[discovered]] that she had been crying.
fixIt.explanationRu: Невольно выдать чувство или факт — betray. Discover значит «обнаружить, найти» что-то новое, а не показать то, что скрываешь.

reply.context: After a job interview, your friend says: "I tried so hard to look calm, but I'm not sure it worked."
options: Why? Did you betray your calm face on purpose?
Why, did your voice betray you? Honestly, everyone gets nervous.
Did your countenance betray any trepidation whatsoever?
reply.explanationRu: Your voice betrayed you — голос невольно выдал волнение. Betray не бывает «нарочно», а третий вариант слишком книжный для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: Her face showed how disappointed she was, although she tried to hide it.
rewrite.frame: Her face ____ her disappointment, although she tried to hide it.
rewrite.explanationRu: Betray — невольно выдать чувство, которое пытаешься скрыть.
